objects.definition: typedef uint8_t fract8;   ///< ANSI: unsigned short _Fract
objects.description: Unsigned 8-bit fixed-point fractional type representing unsigned 256ths (range ~0.0 to 0.99609375, step 1/256). Backed by uint8_t.

objects.definition: typedef int8_t sfract7;  ///< ANSI: signed   short _Fract
objects.description: Signed 8-bit fixed-point fractional type representing signed 1/128 steps (range about -0.9921875 to 0.9921875). Backed by int8_t.
Unsigned 16-bit fixed-point fractional type representing unsigned 1/65536 steps (range ~0.0 to 0.99998474121). Backed by uint16_t.
Signed 16-bit fixed-point fractional type representing signed 1/32768 steps (range about -0.99996948242 to 0.99996948242). Backed by int16_t.

objects.definition: typedef uint16_t accum88;    ///< ANSI: unsigned short _Accum.  8 bits int, 8 bits fraction
objects.description: Unsigned 16-bit fixed-point accumulator with 8 integer bits and 8 fractional bits (Q8.8). Used for BPM88 and similar quantities.

objects.definition: typedef int16_t  saccum78;   ///< ANSI: signed   short _Accum.  7 bits int, 8 bits fraction
objects.description: Signed 16-bit fixed-point accumulator with 7 integer bits and 8 fractional bits (Q7.8).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t accum1616;  ///< ANSI: signed         _Accum. 16 bits int, 16 bits fraction
objects.description: Unsigned 32-bit fixed-point accumulator with 16 integer bits and 16 fractional bits (Q16.16). Note: comment says "signed" but the underlying type is uint32_t, so it's unsigned.

objects.definition: typedef int32_t  saccum1516; ///< ANSI: signed         _Accum. 15 bits int, 16 bits fraction
objects.description: Signed 32-bit fixed-point accumulator with 15 integer bits and 16 fractional bits (Q15.16).

objects.definition: typedef uint16_t accum124;   ///< no direct ANSI counterpart. 12 bits int, 4 bits fraction
objects.description: Unsigned 16-bit fixed-point accumulator with 12 integer bits and 4 fractional bits (Q12.4).

objects.definition: typedef int32_t  saccum114;  ///< no direct ANSI counterpart. 1 bit int, 14 bits fraction
objects.description: Signed 32-bit fixed-point accumulator with 1 integer bit and 14 fractional bits (Q1.14 stored in 32-bit int).

Union exposing IEEE-754 binary32 (float) internals. Provides access to the raw 32-bit integer representation and bitfields for sign, exponent, and mantissa in multiple layouts. Useful for low-level float manipulation or inspection.

Packed 24-bit RGB color struct holding three 8-bit channels (r/g/b). Anonymous unions provide alternate member names red/green/blue. Used throughout the header as the color value for arithmetic, scaling, blending, and conversions to/from 24-bit codes. Trivially copyable POD; no special construction or destruction required.

Enumeration selecting how hue distance is measured when blending/interpolating HSV colors. Values indicate forward wrap, backward wrap, shortest path, or longest path around the hue circle. Used by blend().

Packed 8-bit-per-channel HSV color structure. Fields are hue (h/hue), saturation (s/sat/saturation), and value/brightness (v/val/value). Provides multiple alias names for convenience. The header also includes helper functions hsv_is_zero() and hsv_from_values() that operate on this type, and the blend() API consumes and returns hsv_t.

objects.definition: typedef size_t (*xy_to_offs_cb)(void *ctx, size_t x, size_t y);
objects.description: Function pointer type for mapping 2D coordinates (x, y) to a linear offset within an LED buffer, with an opaque context pointer. Applications must provide an implementation when using blur2d/rows/columns APIs.

functions.name: sfract15ToFloat
functions.signature: static inline float sfract15ToFloat(sfract15 y)
functions.description: Converts a signed 16-bit fixed-point value in sfract15 format (range approximately -1.0 to +1.0, where 1.0 is not representable) to a 32-bit IEEE754 float by dividing by 32768.0. Use when you need floating-point math from fixed-point inputs.
requirements: Argument y must be an sfract15 (int16_t) representing a value in approximately (-1.0, 1.0).
Result is approximate due to floating-point precision; 1.0 and -1.0 are not exactly representable in sfract15.

functions.name: floatToSfract15
functions.signature: static inline sfract15 floatToSfract15(float f)
functions.description: Converts a 32-bit IEEE754 float in the range (-1.0, 1.0) to a signed 16-bit fixed-point sfract15 by multiplying by 32768.0. Useful for preparing float values for lib8tion fixed-point operations.
requirements: Input f should be in the range (-1.0, 1.0); the exact extremes ±1.0 are not representable in sfract15 and will overflow if provided.
Callers should clamp or validate f to within the representable range before conversion if needed.

functions.name: lerp8by8
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t lerp8by8(uint8_t a, uint8_t b, fract8 frac)
functions.description: Linearly interpolates between two 8-bit unsigned values using an 8-bit fractional weight (0..255) without promoting to wider types. Equivalent to a + ((b - a) * frac) / 256.
requirements: a and b are 8-bit unsigned values (0..255).
frac is fract8 (0..255), where 0 yields a and 255 approaches b (off-by-1 per 1/256 scaling).

functions.name: lerp16by16
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t lerp16by16(uint16_t a, uint16_t b, fract16 frac)
functions.description: Linearly interpolates between two 16-bit unsigned values using a 16-bit fractional weight (0..65535). Equivalent to a + ((b - a) * frac) / 65536.
requirements: a and b are 16-bit unsigned values (0..65535).
frac is fract16 (0..65535), where 0 yields a and 65535 approaches b.

functions.name: lerp16by8
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t lerp16by8(uint16_t a, uint16_t b, fract8 frac)
functions.description: Linearly interpolates between two 16-bit unsigned values using an 8-bit fractional weight (0..255). Uses scale16by8 for efficiency.
requirements: a and b are 16-bit unsigned values (0..65535).
frac is fract8 (0..255), where 0 yields a and 255 approaches b.

functions.name: lerp15by8
functions.signature: static inline int16_t lerp15by8(int16_t a, int16_t b, fract8 frac)
functions.description: Linearly interpolates between two signed 16-bit values (intended for signed 15-bit magnitude) using an 8-bit fractional weight. Uses scale16by8 internally.
requirements: a and b are int16_t values. The comments refer to 'signed 15-bit values'; keep inputs within int16_t range.
frac is fract8 (0..255), where 0 yields a and 255 approaches b.

functions.name: lerp15by16
functions.signature: static inline int16_t lerp15by16(int16_t a, int16_t b, fract16 frac)
functions.description: Linearly interpolates between two signed 16-bit values using a 16-bit fractional weight (0..65535). Uses scale16 internally.
requirements: a and b are int16_t values.
frac is fract16 (0..65535), where 0 yields a and 65535 approaches b.

functions.name: map8
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t map8(uint8_t in, uint8_t rangeStart, uint8_t rangeEnd)
functions.description: Maps a full-range 8-bit input (0..255) into a sub-range [rangeStart, rangeEnd] using 8-bit scaling. Similar to Arduino map(in,0,255,rangeStart,rangeEnd) but optimized for 8-bit arithmetic.
requirements: rangeStart and rangeEnd are 0..255.
To avoid unsigned underflow in internal subtraction, ensure rangeEnd >= rangeStart.

functions.name: ease8InOutQuad
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t ease8InOutQuad(uint8_t i)
functions.description: 8-bit quadratic ease-in/ease-out shaping function producing an S-curve. Useful for smoothing transitions such as LED brightness changes.
requirements: i is 0..255. No other constraints.

functions.name: ease16InOutQuad
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t ease16InOutQuad(uint16_t i)
functions.description: 16-bit quadratic ease-in/ease-out shaping function producing an S-curve, analogous to ease8InOutQuad but with 16-bit resolution.
requirements: i is 0..65535. No other constraints.

functions.name: ease8InOutCubic
functions.signature: static inline fract8 ease8InOutCubic(fract8 i)
functions.description: 8-bit cubic ease-in/ease-out shaping function. More pronounced S-curve than quadratic. Returns values in 0..255 and saturates at 255 if intermediate math reaches 256.
requirements: i is fract8 (0..255).

functions.name: ease8InOutApprox
functions.signature: static inline fract8 ease8InOutApprox(fract8 i)
functions.description: Fast, approximate 8-bit ease-in/ease-out function shaped similarly to ease8InOutCubic but with lower computational cost. Error is within a few percent of cubic.
requirements: i is fract8 (0..255). Precision is approximate by design.

functions.name: triwave8
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t triwave8(uint8_t in)
functions.description: Generates a triangle wave from a monotonically increasing 8-bit input. Output rises 0..254 for inputs 0..127, then falls 254..0 for inputs 128..255.
requirements: in is 0..255. No other constraints.

functions.name: quadwave8
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t quadwave8(uint8_t in)
functions.description: Generates an S-shaped quadratic waveform by applying ease8InOutQuad to a triangle wave of the input. Useful for smooth oscillations.

functions.name: cubicwave8
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t cubicwave8(uint8_t in)
functions.description: Generates an S-shaped cubic waveform by applying ease8InOutCubic to a triangle wave of the input. Spends more time near the extrema than sine.

functions.name: squarewave8
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t squarewave8(uint8_t in, uint8_t pulsewidth)
functions.description: Generates a square wave: returns 255 when in < pulsewidth (or pulsewidth == 255), else 0. Pulse width controls duty cycle.
requirements: in and pulsewidth are 0..255.
If pulsewidth == 255, output is always 255.
For pulsewidth < 255, output is 255 when in < pulsewidth, else 0.

functions.name: beat88
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t beat88(accum88 beats_per_minute_88, uint32_t timebase)
functions.description: Generates a 16-bit sawtooth wave that advances at the given BPM specified in Q8.8 fixed-point (e.g., 120 BPM => 120*256). Uses milliseconds-since-boot and a timebase to compute phase.
requirements: beats_per_minute_88 must be BPM in Q8.8 fixed-point (accum88).
timebase must be in the same time units/epoch as GET_MILLIS() (milliseconds since boot on ESP). Pass 0 for phase starting at boot or GET_MILLIS() for phase reset now.
BPM accuracy is approximate (~0.05%).

functions.name: beat16
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t beat16(accum88 beats_per_minute, uint32_t timebase)
functions.description: Generates a 16-bit sawtooth wave advancing at the given BPM. Accepts either a simple 8-bit integer BPM (1..255) or a Q8.8 accum88; simple values are auto-promoted.
requirements: beats_per_minute may be 1..255 (interpreted as integer BPM) or Q8.8 (>=256).
timebase must be in the same units/epoch as GET_MILLIS() (milliseconds since boot).

functions.name: beat8
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t beat8(accum88 beats_per_minute, uint32_t timebase)
functions.description: Generates an 8-bit sawtooth wave at the given BPM. Equivalent to the high byte of beat16.
requirements: beats_per_minute may be 1..255 (integer BPM) or Q8.8 (>=256).
timebase must be in the same units/epoch as GET_MILLIS() (milliseconds since boot).

functions.name: beatsin88
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t beatsin88(accum88 beats_per_minute_88, uint16_t lowest, uint16_t highest, uint32_t timebase, uint16_t phase_offset)
functions.description: Generates a 16-bit sine wave oscillating between [lowest, highest] at the given BPM in Q8.8. phase_offset shifts the sine phase. Implemented as scaled sin16 of the beat phase.
requirements: beats_per_minute_88 must be Q8.8 BPM (e.g., 120*256).
lowest and highest are uint16_t bounds; to avoid unsigned underflow in (highest - lowest), ensure highest >= lowest.
timebase must share the GET_MILLIS() epoch/units (milliseconds since boot).
phase_offset is a 16-bit angle added to the internal phase.

functions.name: beatsin16
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t beatsin16(accum88 beats_per_minute, uint16_t lowest, uint16_t highest, uint32_t timebase, uint16_t phase_offset)
functions.description: Generates a 16-bit sine wave oscillating between [lowest, highest] at the given BPM. Accepts integer BPM (1..255) or Q8.8. phase_offset shifts the phase.
requirements: beats_per_minute may be 1..255 (integer BPM) or Q8.8.
lowest and highest are uint16_t; ensure highest >= lowest to avoid underflow.
timebase must share the GET_MILLIS() epoch/units (milliseconds since boot).
phase_offset is a 16-bit angle.

functions.name: beatsin8
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t beatsin8(accum88 beats_per_minute, uint8_t lowest, uint8_t highest, uint32_t timebase, uint8_t phase_offset)
functions.description: Generates an 8-bit sine wave oscillating between [lowest, highest] at the given BPM. Accepts integer BPM (1..255) or Q8.8. phase_offset shifts the phase.
requirements: beats_per_minute may be 1..255 (integer BPM) or Q8.8.
lowest and highest are uint8_t; ensure highest >= lowest to avoid underflow in (highest - lowest).
timebase must share the GET_MILLIS() epoch/units (milliseconds since boot).
phase_offset is an 8-bit angle.

functions.name: seconds16
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t seconds16()
functions.description: Returns seconds since boot as a 16-bit value (truncates/wraps at 65535). Useful for time-periodic operations.
requirements: No arguments. Relies on GET_MILLIS() which must be available (esp_timer based).
Wraps approximately every 65536 seconds (~18.2 hours).

functions.name: minutes16
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t minutes16()
functions.description: Returns minutes since boot as a 16-bit value (wraps at 65535). Computed from GET_MILLIS().
requirements: No arguments. Relies on GET_MILLIS() which must be available.
Wraps approximately every 65535 minutes (~45.5 days).

functions.name: hours8
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t hours8()
functions.description: Returns hours since boot as an 8-bit value (wraps at 255). Computed from GET_MILLIS().
requirements: No arguments. Relies on GET_MILLIS() which must be available.
Wraps every 256 hours (~10.7 days).

functions.name: div1024_32_16
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t div1024_32_16(uint32_t in32)
functions.description: Divides a 32-bit value by 1024 using a right-shift by 10 and returns the low 16 bits. Used to convert milliseconds to 'binary seconds' (1 bsecond = 1024 ms).
requirements: in32 is any uint32_t. The high bits beyond the low 16 after shifting are discarded.

functions.name: bseconds16
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t bseconds16()
functions.description: Returns time since boot in 'binary seconds' (units of 1024 milliseconds) as a 16-bit value. Computed from GET_MILLIS() via div1024_32_16.
requirements: No arguments. Relies on GET_MILLIS() which must be available.
Wraps at 65535 bseconds (~18.6 hours).

functions.name: rgb_is_zero
functions.signature: static inline bool rgb_is_zero(rgb_t a)
functions.description: Returns true if all three channels of the given rgb_t color are zero. Intended for quick checks for black/off pixels.
requirements: Argument a must be a valid rgb_t struct.

functions.name: rgb_from_code
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_from_code(uint32_t color_code)
functions.description: Constructs an rgb_t from a 24-bit color code formatted as 0x00RRGGBB (red in bits 16–23, green in bits 8–15, blue in bits 0–7).
requirements: color_code is interpreted as 0x00RRGGBB; higher bits beyond the low 24 are ignored.
Caller must include a valid 24-bit RGB value if a specific color is intended.

functions.name: rgb_from_values
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_from_values(uint8_t r, uint8_t g, uint8_t b)
functions.description: Constructs an rgb_t from separate 8-bit red, green, and blue channel values.
requirements: Each channel value r, g, b must be in the range 0..255.

functions.name: rgb_to_code
functions.signature: static inline uint32_t rgb_to_code(rgb_t color)
functions.description: Packs an rgb_t into a 24-bit color code formatted as 0x00RRGGBB.
requirements: Argument color must be a valid rgb_t struct.

functions.name: rgb_add
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_add(rgb_t a, uint8_t val)
functions.description: Adds the same 8-bit value to each channel of the color with saturation at 0xFF. Uses qadd8 from lib8tion for per-channel saturated addition.
requirements: Requires qadd8 from lib8tion.h to be available.
val should be in the range 0..255.

functions.name: rgb_sub
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_sub(rgb_t a, uint8_t val)
functions.description: Subtracts the same 8-bit value from each channel of the color with saturation at 0x00. Uses qsub8 from lib8tion.
requirements: Requires qsub8 from lib8tion.h to be available.
val should be in the range 0..255.

functions.name: rgb_mul
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_mul(rgb_t a, uint8_t val)
functions.description: Multiplies each channel by an 8-bit value with 8-bit scaling and saturation to 0xFF using qmul8 from lib8tion.
requirements: Requires qmul8 from lib8tion.h to be available.
val should be in the range 0..255.

functions.name: rgb_add_rgb
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_add_rgb(rgb_t a, rgb_t b)
functions.description: Per-channel saturated addition of two colors, clamping each result at 0xFF. Uses qadd8 per channel.
requirements: Requires qadd8 from lib8tion.h to be available.
Inputs a and b must be valid rgb_t structs.

functions.name: rgb_sub_rgb
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_sub_rgb(rgb_t a, rgb_t b)
functions.description: Per-channel saturated subtraction of color b from color a, clamping each result at 0x00. Uses qsub8 per channel.
requirements: Requires qsub8 from lib8tion.h to be available.
Inputs a and b must be valid rgb_t structs.

functions.name: rgb_scale
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_scale(rgb_t a, uint8_t scaledown)
functions.description: Scales each channel by scaledown/256 using scale8 from lib8tion ("plain math" dimming). At low levels channels may reach 0.
requirements: Requires scale8 from lib8tion.h to be available.
scaledown should be in the range 0..255.

functions.name: rgb_scale_video
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_scale_video(rgb_t a, uint8_t scaledown)
functions.description: Scales each channel by scaledown/256 using scale8_video ("video" dimming), which prevents nonzero channels from becoming zero unless scaledown is 0.
requirements: Requires scale8_video from lib8tion.h to be available.
scaledown should be in the range 0..255.

functions.name: rgb_fade_light
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_fade_light(rgb_t a, uint8_t fade_factor)
functions.description: Lightens/dims a color using video-scaling with factor (255 - fade_factor). Equivalent to rgb_scale_video(a, 255 - fade_factor).
requirements: Requires scale8_video from lib8tion.h to be available (via rgb_scale_video).
fade_factor should be in the range 0..255.

functions.name: rgb_fade
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_fade(rgb_t a, uint8_t fade_factor)
functions.description: Dims a color using plain scaling with factor (255 - fade_factor). Equivalent to rgb_scale(a, 255 - fade_factor).
requirements: Requires scale8 from lib8tion.h to be available (via rgb_scale).
fade_factor should be in the range 0..255.

functions.name: rgb_invert
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_invert(rgb_t a)
functions.description: Inverts each channel (bitwise NOT) producing 255 - channel for 8-bit values, yielding the color complement.
requirements: Argument a must be a valid rgb_t struct.

functions.name: rgb_luma
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t rgb_luma(rgb_t a)
functions.description: Computes an 8-bit luma estimate using weighted sum: 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B approximated with scale8 weights (54, 183, 18).
requirements: Requires scale8 from lib8tion.h to be available.

functions.name: rgb_average_light
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t rgb_average_light(rgb_t a)
functions.description: Computes the simple average of R, G, and B using scale8 with weight 85 (i.e., approximately (R+G+B)/3).
requirements: Requires scale8 from lib8tion.h to be available.

functions.name: rgb_max_brightness
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_max_brightness(rgb_t a, uint8_t limit)
functions.description: Scales the color so its maximum channel equals limit (0..255), preserving ratios. If the color is black (all zero), returns it unchanged.
requirements: limit should be in the range 0..255.
No division by zero occurs; function early-returns when a is black.
Argument a must be a valid rgb_t.

functions.name: rgb_lerp8
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_lerp8(rgb_t a, rgb_t b, fract8 frac)
functions.description: Linearly interpolates between colors a and b by an 8-bit fraction using lerp8by8 per channel. frac=0 yields a; frac=255 yields approximately b.
requirements: Requires lerp8by8 from lib8tion.h to be available.
frac must be a valid fract8 (0..255).
Arguments a and b must be valid rgb_t structs.

functions.name: rgb_lerp16
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_lerp16(rgb_t a, rgb_t b, fract16 frac)
functions.description: Linearly interpolates between colors a and b by a 16-bit fraction using lerp16by16 per channel; results truncated to 8-bit per channel.
requirements: Requires lerp16by16 from lib8tion.h to be available.
frac must be a valid fract16 (0..65535).
Arguments a and b must be valid rgb_t structs.

functions.name: rgb_blend
functions.signature: static inline rgb_t rgb_blend(rgb_t existing, rgb_t overlay, fract8 amount)
functions.description: Blends overlay onto existing by an 8-bit amount using blend8 per channel. amount=0 keeps existing; amount=255 gives overlay.
requirements: Requires blend8 from lib8tion.h to be available.
amount must be a valid fract8 (0..255).
Arguments existing and overlay must be valid rgb_t structs.

functions.name: hsv_is_zero
functions.signature: static inline bool hsv_is_zero(hsv_t a)
functions.description: Returns true if the provided HSV color has all components equal to zero (h == 0, s == 0, v == 0), otherwise false. Useful for quickly checking if a color is effectively "off" or uninitialized. Pure function with no side effects.
requirements: Parameter a must be an initialized hsv_t value.
No side effects or resource requirements are involved.

functions.name: hsv_from_values
functions.signature: static inline hsv_t hsv_from_values(uint8_t h, uint8_t s, uint8_t v)
functions.description: Constructs and returns an hsv_t from the provided hue, saturation, and value bytes. Intended for creating HSV colors where each component uses an 8-bit range.
requirements: Parameters h, s, and v are uint8_t values and should be in the range 0–255.
No additional initialization is required; the function returns a fully formed hsv_t.

functions.name: blend
functions.signature: hsv_t blend(hsv_t existing, hsv_t overlay, fract8 amount, color_gradient_direction_t direction)
functions.description: Computes and returns a new HSV color by blending between existing and overlay by a fractional amount. The hue blending path is controlled by direction (forward, backward, shortest, or longest arc around the hue wheel). Typical usage: supply two hsv_t colors, a fractional amount (fract8), and a hue-gradient direction to obtain an interpolated color. Exact interpolation details (e.g., gamma, wrap behavior) follow the library’s implementation; amount is commonly interpreted such that 0 yields existing and 255 yields overlay.
requirements: Parameters existing and overlay must be initialized hsv_t colors.
Parameter amount is of type fract8 (typically an 8-bit fraction in the range 0–255).
Parameter direction must be one of the color_gradient_direction_t enum values: COLOR_FORWARD_HUES, COLOR_BACKWARD_HUES, COLOR_SHORTEST_HUES, or COLOR_LONGEST_HUES.

Function returns an hsv_t; callers should handle the returned value appropriately. Other behavioral details (e.g., exact mapping of amount or hue wrap strategy) are library-defined and not specified in this header.

functions.name: hsv2rgb_rainbow
functions.signature: rgb_t hsv2rgb_rainbow(hsv_t hsv);
functions.description: Convert an HSV color to RGB using a visually balanced rainbow mapping (better yellows/oranges than a straight spectrum). Hue is treated as 0–255. Use when you want perceptually balanced rainbow colors.
requirements: hsv.hsv must be a valid hsv_t value with components in their expected 8-bit ranges (h: 0–255, s: 0–255, v: 0–255)
No other preconditions are specified

functions.name: hsv2rgb_spectrum
functions.signature: rgb_t hsv2rgb_spectrum(hsv_t hsv);
functions.description: Convert an HSV color to RGB using a mathematically straight spectrum mapping (more green/blue, less yellow/orange vs rainbow). Hue is 0–255.
requirements: hsv.hsv must be a valid hsv_t value with components in their expected 8-bit ranges (h: 0–255, s: 0–255, v: 0–255)

functions.name: hsv2rgb_raw
functions.signature: rgb_t hsv2rgb_raw(hsv_t hsv);
functions.description: Convert HSV to RGB using a faster, less balanced spectrum algorithm that expects hue in 0–191. Useful when speed matters more than color balance.
requirements: hsv.h must be in range 0–191 (HUE_MAX_RAW)
hsv.s and hsv.v should be in 0–255
Passing hue outside 0–191 is unspecified

functions.name: rgb2hsv_approximate
functions.signature: hsv_t rgb2hsv_approximate(rgb_t rgb);
functions.description: Approximate conversion from RGB to HSV. Optimized to recover hue well for fully saturated colors originating from HSV; results are approximate, especially for desaturated inputs.
requirements: rgb must be a valid rgb_t value with 8-bit channel components (0–255)
Accuracy is not guaranteed; caller must tolerate approximation

functions.name: rgb_heat_color
functions.signature: rgb_t rgb_heat_color(uint8_t temperature);
functions.description: Map a heat value (0 cool … 255 hot) to an RGB color approximating black-body radiation for fire-like effects. Fast and compact, not chromatically exact.
requirements: temperature should be in 0–255
Behavior for values outside 0–255 is unspecified

functions.name: hsv_fill_solid_hsv
functions.signature: void hsv_fill_solid_hsv(hsv_t *target, hsv_t color, size_t num);
functions.description: Fill an array of HSV colors with a single HSV color.
requirements: target must point to an array with at least num elements
If num is 0, the function performs no writes
color must be a valid hsv_t

functions.name: rgb_fill_solid_hsv
functions.signature: void rgb_fill_solid_hsv(rgb_t *target, hsv_t color, size_t num);
functions.description: Fill an RGB array with a solid color specified in HSV; each element is converted to RGB.
requirements: target must point to an array with at least num elements
If num is 0, no writes occur
color must be a valid hsv_t

functions.name: rgb_fill_solid_rgb
functions.signature: void rgb_fill_solid_rgb(rgb_t *target, rgb_t color, size_t num);
functions.description: Fill an RGB array with a single RGB color.
requirements: target must point to an array with at least num elements
If num is 0, no writes occur
color must be a valid rgb_t

functions.name: hsv_fill_gradient_hsv
functions.signature: void hsv_fill_gradient_hsv(hsv_t *target, size_t startpos, hsv_t startcolor, size_t endpos, hsv_t endcolor, color_gradient_direction_t direction);
functions.description: Fill a span of an HSV array with a smooth HSV gradient between two HSV colors. Direction controls how hue wraps around the color wheel (FORWARD_HUES, BACKWARD_HUES, SHORTEST_HUES, LONGEST_HUES).
requirements: target must reference an array large enough to cover indices [startpos, endpos]
startpos and endpos must be valid indices into target, with startpos <= endpos
direction must be one of the defined color_gradient_direction_t values (FORWARD_HUES, BACKWARD_HUES, SHORTEST_HUES, LONGEST_HUES)
startcolor and endcolor must be valid hsv_t values

functions.name: hsv_fill_gradient2_hsv
functions.signature: static inline void hsv_fill_gradient2_hsv(hsv_t *target, size_t num, hsv_t c1, hsv_t c2, color_gradient_direction_t direction)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to fill an HSV array with a gradient from c1 to c2 across the entire array (calls hsv_fill_gradient_hsv with start at 0 and end at num-1).
requirements: target must point to an array with at least num elements
num must be >= 1 (uses index num - 1)
direction must be a valid color_gradient_direction_t
c1 and c2 must be valid hsv_t values

functions.name: hsv_fill_gradient3_hsv
functions.signature: static inline void hsv_fill_gradient3_hsv(hsv_t *target, size_t num, hsv_t c1, hsv_t c2, hsv_t c3, color_gradient_direction_t direction)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to fill an HSV array with a two-segment gradient: c1→c2 over first half, then c2→c3 over second half.
requirements: target must point to an array with at least num elements
num must be >= 1 (uses indices 0, num/2, and num-1)
direction must be a valid color_gradient_direction_t
c1, c2, c3 must be valid hsv_t values

functions.name: hsv_fill_gradient4_hsv
functions.signature: static inline void hsv_fill_gradient4_hsv(hsv_t *target, size_t num, hsv_t c1, hsv_t c2, hsv_t c3, hsv_t c4, color_gradient_direction_t direction)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to fill an HSV array with a three-segment gradient: c1→c2 over first third, c2→c3 over second third, c3→c4 over final third.
requirements: target must point to an array with at least num elements
num must be >= 1 (uses indices 0, num/3, 2*num/3, and num-1)
direction must be a valid color_gradient_direction_t
c1, c2, c3, c4 must be valid hsv_t values

functions.name: rgb_fill_gradient_hsv
functions.signature: void rgb_fill_gradient_hsv(rgb_t *target, size_t startpos, hsv_t startcolor, size_t endpos, hsv_t endcolor, color_gradient_direction_t direction);
functions.description: Fill a span of an RGB array with a gradient computed in HSV space between two HSV colors; each interpolated HSV is converted to RGB as written. Hue sweep direction is controlled as with HSV gradients.
requirements: target must reference an array large enough to cover indices [startpos, endpos]
startpos and endpos must be valid indices, with startpos <= endpos
direction must be a valid color_gradient_direction_t value
startcolor and endcolor must be valid hsv_t values

functions.name: color_from_palette_hsv
functions.signature: hsv_t color_from_palette_hsv(const hsv_t *palette, uint8_t pal_size, uint8_t index, uint8_t brightness, bool blend);
functions.description: Lookup an HSV color by 0–255 index from an HSV palette of pal_size explicit entries. Entries are evenly distributed over 0–255; intermediate values are HSV-interpolated between adjacent entries when blending is enabled.
requirements: palette must point to at least pal_size hsv_t entries
pal_size must be >= 1
index is used over 0–255 domain
brightness is 0–255
blend specifies whether to interpolate between entries; must be a valid boolean

functions.name: color_from_palette_rgb
functions.signature: rgb_t color_from_palette_rgb(const rgb_t *palette, uint8_t pal_size, uint8_t index, uint8_t brightness, bool blend);
functions.description: Lookup an RGB color by 0–255 index from an RGB palette of pal_size explicit entries. Entries are evenly spread over 0–255; intermediate values are interpolated in RGB (respecting blend flag).
requirements: palette must point to at least pal_size rgb_t entries
pal_size must be >= 1
index is used over 0–255 domain
brightness is 0–255
blend must be a valid boolean

functions.name: blur1d
functions.signature: void blur1d(rgb_t *leds, size_t num_leds, fract8 blur_amount);
functions.description: Apply a one-dimensional blur that spreads light to two neighboring LEDs. 0 = no blur; ~64 = moderate; 172 = maximum even spreading; 173–255 = wider but may flicker. Repeated application also fades overall brightness.
requirements: leds must point to an array with at least num_leds elements
num_leds is the number of elements to process
blur_amount is a fract8 (0–255). Values >172 may introduce flicker as noted
Function does not conserve total light; caller should expect cumulative fading across repeated calls

functions.name: blur_columns
functions.signature: void blur_columns(rgb_t *leds, size_t width, size_t height, fract8 blur_amount, xy_to_offs_cb xy, void *ctx);
functions.description: Apply blur1d to each column of a width×height matrix. Element order is provided by the xy-to-offset callback, which maps (x,y) to a linear index in leds.
requirements: leds must point to an array with at least width*height elements
width and height specify the matrix dimensions and must be consistent with leds
blur_amount is 0–255 as fract8
xy must be a non-null callback mapping valid 0<=x<width, 0<=y<height to a valid index in [0, width*height)
ctx is an opaque pointer passed through to xy

functions.name: blur_rows
functions.signature: void blur_rows(rgb_t *leds, size_t width, size_t height, fract8 blur_amount, xy_to_offs_cb xy, void *ctx);
functions.description: Apply blur1d to each row of a width×height matrix. The xy callback maps (x,y) to a linear index in leds for row traversal.
requirements: leds must point to an array with at least width*height elements
width and height specify the matrix dimensions and must be consistent with leds
blur_amount is 0–255 as fract8
xy must be a non-null callback mapping valid 0<=x<width, 0<=y<height to a valid index in [0, width*height)
ctx is an opaque pointer passed through to xy

functions.name: blur2d
functions.signature: void blur2d(rgb_t *leds, size_t width, size_t height, fract8 blur_amount, xy_to_offs_cb xy, void *ctx);
functions.description: Apply a two-dimensional blur that spreads light to up to eight neighboring pixels on a width×height matrix. Repeated application also fades overall brightness.
requirements: leds must point to an array with at least width*height elements
width and height specify the matrix dimensions and must be consistent with leds
blur_amount is a fract8 (0–255). Values >172 may introduce flicker as noted for blur filters
xy must be a non-null callback mapping valid 0<=x<width, 0<=y<height to a valid index in [0, width*height)
ctx is an opaque pointer passed through to xy

functions.name: apply_gamma2brightness
functions.signature: uint8_t apply_gamma2brightness(uint8_t brightness, float gamma);
functions.description: Apply gamma correction to a single 8-bit brightness value. Useful for perceptual linearization for LEDs.
requirements: brightness is 0–255
gamma is a floating-point correction factor; typical values > 0 (e.g., 1.8–2.8). Exact valid range is not specified in this header

functions.name: apply_gamma2rgb
functions.signature: rgb_t apply_gamma2rgb(rgb_t c, float gamma);
functions.description: Apply the same gamma correction to each channel of an RGB color.
requirements: c must be a valid rgb_t with 8-bit channels
gamma is a floating-point correction factor; exact range is unspecified

functions.name: apply_gamma2rgb_channels
functions.signature: rgb_t apply_gamma2rgb_channels(rgb_t c, float gamma_r, float gamma_g, float gamma_b);
functions.description: Apply per-channel gamma corrections to an RGB color using separate gamma values for R, G, and B.
requirements: c must be a valid rgb_t with 8-bit channels
gamma_r, gamma_g, gamma_b are floating-point correction factors; exact valid ranges are unspecified

functions.name: inoise16_3d
functions.signature: uint16_t inoise16_3d(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t z);
functions.description: Returns a 16-bit, fixed-point Perlin noise value sampled at 3D coordinates. Coordinates are 16.16 fixed-point packed into 32-bit integers. Output is scaled to the full unsigned 16-bit range [0, 65535]. Typical usage: pass x,y,z as advancing 16.16 positions to obtain smoothly varying noise for animation or textures.
requirements: x, y, z are 16.16 fixed-point coordinates encoded in uint32_t (high 16 bits integer part, low 16 bits fractional).
Function returns an unsigned value scaled to the range 0..65535.
No side effects; can be called repeatedly with any coordinates.

functions.name: inoise16_2d
functions.signature: uint16_t inoise16_2d(uint32_t x, uint32_t y);
functions.description: Returns a 16-bit, fixed-point Perlin noise value sampled at 2D coordinates. Coordinates are 16.16 fixed-point in 32-bit integers. Output is scaled to [0, 65535]. Useful for 2D textures and patterns over a grid of x,y positions.
requirements: x and y are 16.16 fixed-point coordinates encoded in uint32_t (high 16 bits integer part, low 16 bits fractional).
Function returns an unsigned value scaled to the range 0..65535.

requirements: x is a 16.16 fixed-point coordinate encoded in uint32_t (high 16 bits integer part, low 16 bits fractional).
Function returns an unsigned value scaled to the range 0..65535.

functions.name: inoise16_3d_raw
functions.signature: int16_t inoise16_3d_raw(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t z);
functions.description: Returns a raw 16-bit Perlin noise sample at 3D coordinates without scaling/offset. Coordinates are 16.16 fixed-point in 32-bit integers. Output is roughly in the range [-18000, 18000] (approximate).
requirements: x, y, z are 16.16 fixed-point coordinates encoded in uint32_t (high 16 bits integer part, low 16 bits fractional).
Return value is a signed 16-bit noise value; magnitude is approximately within ±18k but not guaranteed.

functions.name: fill_raw_noise8
functions.signature: void fill_raw_noise8(uint8_t *pData, uint8_t num_points, uint8_t octaves, uint16_t x, int scale, uint16_t time);
functions.description: Fills a 1D array with raw 8-bit noise values computed along the x axis, using one or more octaves. Coordinates use the 8.8 fixed-point convention (x and time are 16-bit). Values written are raw (not scaled/offset beyond the noise function’s native raw output). Suitable for generating noise sequences for LEDs or textures.
requirements: pData must be a valid, writable pointer to a buffer of at least num_points bytes.
num_points specifies how many samples will be written starting at pData[0].
octaves selects the number of noise octaves to combine; exact range/behavior is not specified in this header (caller should choose a small positive integer).
x is an 8.8 fixed-point start coordinate in uint16_t (high 8 bits integer part, low 8 bits fractional).
scale controls spacing between successive x samples when filling; exact units and valid range are not specified here.
time is an 8.8 fixed-point coordinate in uint16_t used as the temporal/third dimension.
Function does not return a value; caller must ensure buffer bounds are not exceeded.

functions.name: fill_raw_noise16into8
functions.signature: void fill_raw_noise16into8(uint8_t *pData, uint8_t num_points, uint8_t octaves, uint32_t x, int scale, uint32_t time);
functions.description: Fills a 1D byte array with values derived from 16-bit raw noise sampled along the x axis, written into 8-bit storage. Coordinates use the 16.16 fixed-point convention (x and time are 32-bit). This is intended to leverage higher-resolution noise and map it into 8-bit output.
requirements: pData must be a valid, writable pointer to a buffer of at least num_points bytes.
num_points specifies how many samples will be written starting at pData[0].
octaves selects the number of noise octaves to combine; exact range/behavior is not specified in this header (caller should choose a small positive integer).
x is a 16.16 fixed-point start coordinate in uint32_t (high 16 bits integer part, low 16 bits fractional).
scale controls spacing between successive x samples when filling; exact units and valid range are not specified here.
time is a 16.16 fixed-point coordinate in uint32_t used as the temporal/third dimension.
Written values are 8-bit; exact mapping from 16-bit raw noise to 8-bit is not specified here.
Function does not return a value; caller must ensure buffer bounds are not exceeded.
